svg.title: Zero false alarms still leave uncertainty about the population FPR
svg.desc: For n independent negative cases with zero observed false positives, the exact one-sided 95 percent binomial upper confidence limit is 1 minus 0.05 to the power 1 over n. The illustrated n values are 3, 12, 17, and 30; their upper limits are about 63.2, 22.1, 16.2, and 9.5 percent. Only at n at least 17 does the limit fall below the assumed one-sixth FPR budget. The sequence illustrates increasing sample size under an artificial zero-error scenario, not an experiment or model measurement.
svg.text: Zero alarms do not imply zero FPR
SYNTHETIC BINOMIAL · INDEPENDENT CASES · NOT A DEPLOYMENT MEASUREMENT
